problem: Robots underuse navigational signs: prior work only classifies fixed sign categories (traffic/indoor signs) or uses sign text as landmarks, and none parses open-vocabulary locations together with their associated directions.
motivation: Signs directly encode privileged top-down information on actions, regions and relations, including for places outside the robot's line of sight, and they fit topo-semantic navigation. Recent VLMs offer open-world reasoning that could handle sign and scene complexity, but no task definition, benchmark or baseline existed.
key_idea: Define navigational sign understanding (detect signs, then parse (location, text/symbol, direction) cues), release a benchmark with metrics, and provide a GroundingDINO + VLM baseline with an OCR filter and depth-based viewpoint alignment for robot deployment.
insight: Specialized open-set detectors beat general VLMs at sign detection (AP@0.50 0.673 vs 0.289), while VLMs do better on cue parsing, with Gemini-2.0-Flash ahead of GPT-4o. Performance falls on crops from in-the-wild detection compared with curated head-on crops, and on human-rated hard signs (~15% success vs ~40%), which supports the need for active viewpoint alignment. Main failure modes are arrow-place association, multi-line names, overcrowded signs and text-symbol combinations.
method: Task definition: detection of navigational signs (bounding boxes, with both location and direction) and recognition of cue tuples (place, text/symbol label, one of 8 directions or None) per sign crop

Dataset: 160 detection images and 205 annotated recognition crops from hospitals, malls, campuses and transit hubs, with metrics of COCO AP/AR, aggregated cue precision/recall, per-sign exact-match success rate, and Precision_sign/Recall_sign
Sign detection: prompt GroundingDINO with 'navigational signs' and crop the resulting boxes

Sign recognition: a structured VLM prompt (GPT-4o or Gemini-2.0-Flash) that extracts locations, extracts arrows, associates them and outputs a list of tuples; symbols matched by CLIP embedding similarity
Sign filter: PaddleOCR (with optional fuzzy matching against known strings) selects frames with text so the expensive detector runs less often
Alignment: Metric3Dv2 monocular depth, plane fit on the sign to get centroid and normal, then servo to a head-on viewpoint (with arm adjustments) on a Spot robot

setting.action_space: servoing to a target pose in front of the sign; no learned navigation policy

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; results are on the paper's own sign-understanding benchmark, not in the canonical list. Main results: GroundingDINO detection AP@[0.50]=0.673 and AR@100=0.890 (Gemini-2.0-Flash: 0.289 and 0.529). Recognition overall success rate (exact text) is 41.6 for Gemini-2.0-Flash and 39.3 for GPT-4o. Full pipeline GroundingDINO+Gemini-2.0-Flash gives Precision_sign 39.3 and Recall_sign 39.0.
results: GroundingDINO detects signs much better than Gemini-2.0-Flash (AR@100 0.890 vs 0.529). Gemini-2.0-Flash recognizes cues slightly better than GPT-4o (per-sign success 41.6 vs 39.3). The best full pipeline (GroundingDINO + Gemini-2.0-Flash) reaches 39.3 sign precision and 39.0 recall, so the task is far from solved.
limitations: Small benchmark (160 detection images, 205 recognition crops), English signs only, and no navigation-task evaluation

The baseline is far from solved (~40% per-sign success) and struggles with arrow association, overcrowded signs and small or distant signs; the robot demo is qualitative only and relies on a cloud VLM over 4G
builds_on: Liang et al. 2020 sign-based navigation policies
